alerts.title: Returned claims are parsed outside the verified JWS payload
alerts.description: A keyed JWS deserialization accepts one payload representation, while returned claims are independently decoded from a compact-token segment. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
alerts.recommendation: Return claims decoded from the verifier payload, or establish equality with that exact payload before returning them.

obligation.required: Return claims decoded from the verifier payload, or establish equality with that exact payload before returning them.
obligation.observed: A keyed JWS deserialization accepts one payload representation, while returned claims are independently decoded from a compact-token segment.
assumptions: The resolved jwcrypto JWS API may accept compact and JSON representations.
A non-null verification key, caller trust boundary and claim use remain runtime assumptions.

alerts.title: HTTP framing length uses permissive integer parsing
alerts.description: A resolved HTTP parser converts a Content-Length or chunk-size value without an observed lexical rejection guard. Python integer conversion accepts extra forms. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
alerts.recommendation: Validate the exact decimal or hexadecimal HTTP length grammar before integer conversion; reject signs, prefixes and whitespace.

obligation.required: Validate the exact decimal or hexadecimal HTTP length grammar before integer conversion; reject signs, prefixes and whitespace.
obligation.observed: A resolved HTTP parser converts a Content-Length or chunk-size value without an observed lexical rejection guard. Python integer conversion accepts extra forms.
assumptions: Only visible dominating guards and resolved HTTP library contracts are modelled; caller filtering remains unverified.
Recognizing a lexical guard does not certify its regular expression or all parser paths.

alerts.title: HMAC key blacklist omits recognized public-key formats
alerts.description: A finite public-key rejection list guards material stored for a resolved HMAC operation, but omits: ssh-ed25519, ssh-dss, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
alerts.recommendation: Use a complete key-format/type boundary before accepting asymmetric representations as HMAC secrets.

obligation.required: Use a complete key-format/type boundary before accepting asymmetric representations as HMAC secrets.
obligation.observed: A finite public-key rejection list guards material stored for a resolved HMAC operation, but omits: ssh-ed25519, ssh-dss, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521.
assumptions: This checks the visible finite blacklist, not all possible key-format parsers or caller restrictions.
Accepting omitted representations and an attacker-relevant verifier configuration require runtime validation.

alerts.title: MCP message validation can terminate its receive loop
alerts.description: A message from a resolved MCP SessionMessage receive stream reaches model_validate without a visible continuing per-message exception boundary. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
alerts.recommendation: Handle malformed-message validation failures inside the receive loop and return a protocol error without terminating unrelated processing.

obligation.required: Handle malformed-message validation failures inside the receive loop and return a protocol error without terminating unrelated processing.
obligation.observed: A message from a resolved MCP SessionMessage receive stream reaches model_validate without a visible continuing per-message exception boundary.
assumptions: The session model/transport contracts and exception behavior require upstream/runtime verification.
Caller restart policies and the impact on other sessions are not inferred.

alerts.title: TLS verification policy is applied after policy-independent pool selection
alerts.description: A resolved urllib3 pool is selected without the per-call verification argument, then a local helper mutates certificate requirements on that selected pool. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
alerts.recommendation: Partition connection pools by verification policy and TLS context before reusing connections.

obligation.required: Partition connection pools by verification policy and TLS context before reusing connections.
obligation.observed: A resolved urllib3 pool is selected without the per-call verification argument, then a local helper mutates certificate requirements on that selected pool.
assumptions: Pool reuse, TLS context caching and call sequences require runtime verification.
Passing policy into selection suppresses this narrow check; correct pool-key construction is not proved.

alerts.title: Weak hash selected; security use unverified
alerts.description: A resolved hashlib call selects sha1 without usedforsecurity=False. Security impact depends on its use; this is not proof of an exploitable collision.
alerts.recommendation: Use a modern hash for integrity and a password KDF for passwords; declare non-security checksum usage explicitly.

alerts.title: Compatibility normalization follows HTML cleaning
alerts.description: Returned HTML derives from a resolved cleaner and is subsequently transformed with NFKC/NFKD normalization, which can introduce markup-significant characters. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
alerts.recommendation: Apply compatibility normalization before HTML parsing/cleaning, or clean the transformed result again before returning it.

obligation.required: Apply compatibility normalization before HTML parsing/cleaning, or clean the transformed result again before returning it.
obligation.observed: Returned HTML derives from a resolved cleaner and is subsequently transformed with NFKC/NFKD normalization, which can introduce markup-significant characters.
assumptions: The cleaner/serializer contracts are statically resolved; returned HTML rendering and attacker control remain caller assumptions.
This checks transformation order, not the completeness of every cleaner policy or DOM mutation.
